blocks.content: Quiz: When does a CSS rule inside @media (max-width: 48rem) { ... } apply?
Tap an option below to answer:
max-width doesn't detect device type, it only measures viewport width. A desktop browser window resized to 300px would trigger it too.
max-width doesn't detect device type, it only measures viewport width. A desktop browser window resized to 300px would trigger it too.
When the viewport width is 48rem or narrower.
max-width means "at this width or less" so the rule applies when the viewport is 48rem or narrower.
max-width means "at this width or less" so the rule applies when the viewport is 48rem or narrower.
It's not an exact match. max-width means "this wide or narrower" so anything up to and including 48rem triggers it.
It's not an exact match. max-width means "this wide or narrower" so anything up to and including 48rem triggers it.
Only when the user has set a small font size.
Font size is a separate CSS concept. @media (max-width) reads the viewport's pixel width, it has nothing to do with what font the user has set.
Font size is a separate CSS concept. @media (max-width) reads the viewport's pixel width, it has nothing to do with what font the user has set.
